column1: # bios-sysvars-r1.tsv -- DUMPBIOS, the served system variables (TASK/BIOS21):
# one peek case per row of class "served" in the contract table
# docs/api/bios/_sysvars-contract.md section 4, with the return class its
# section 8 maps the row to; the cells TASK/BIOS20 serves take their class
# Form: docs/TOS-REFERENCE-DUMPER.md section 6, "System variables: the peek
# case".  peek:<addr>:<width> reads one cell (width 1, 2 or 4 bytes, the
# cell's own type) inside a Supexec callback: on EmuTOS a user-mode read
# below $800 is a bus error.  Read-only by construction (the guard in
# tosdump/core/cases.c parse_peek_case).  The value is recorded zero-extended
# from its width.  MONOTONE: the cell read twice with two Vsync calls between,
# the second read later than the first (per side, never by value).
# A row's size in the contract table is its width here; _themd (16 bytes) is
# read as its four LONGs (the m68k MD: m_link, m_start, m_length, m_own), and
# ____md (4 bytes) as one LONG.  Address cells are PTR_RAM (non-null, even,
# >= 0x400, < 0x80000000), never compared by value: ROM, stub and buffer
# addresses differ by design.  The "hardware", "missing", "free" and "n/a"
# rows have no case (section 8: a documented-difference case for them is the
# A separate table, so bios-r1.tsv, bios-core-r1.tsv and their references stay
# as they are.  One table per round: the case id is the physical line number
# and the dump header carries the CRC of this file, so it is frozen once
# ---- $420-$43A memory magic and bounds -- bios/memory.S:572-586, biosmem.c
# ---- $442-$44E timer, boot device, screen -- bios/mfp.c:196, bios/bios.c
# ---- $48E _themd, the m68k MD as four LONGs -- bios/biosmem.c:144-147
